facts.text: Underground coal workers reported a higher frequency of jarring and jolting incidents and concern about the forceful nature of stops associated with proximity detection systems; operator-injury risk was reported, not measured.
facts.quote: Underground coal workers report "a higher frequency of jarring and jolting incidents" and concern about "the forceful nature of these stops" [11].

facts.text: Mine leaders described sudden stops with early PDS integrations and preferred a variable-frequency-drive machine integration that substantially reduced speed, slowed to a crawl, and only then set the brake rather than stopping abruptly.
facts.quote: preferred an integration with a variable-frequency-drive machine that first reduced speed substantially, slowed to a crawl and only then set the brake, "not an abrupt stop" [12].

facts.text: MSHA stated in 2017 that it was not aware of any on-board operator injuries resulting from a proximity detection system decelerating or stopping a mobile machine, conflicting with workers' concerns about forceful stops.
facts.quote: **Conflict:** MSHA (2017) is "not aware of any on-board operator injuries resulting from a proximity detection system decelerating and/or stopping a mobile machine" [22].

facts.text: No injury threshold or safe jerk limit for haul trucks, loaders or dozers, and no validated occupant-injury curve for automatic-braking events, was found.
facts.quote: No injury threshold or safe jerk limit for haul trucks, loaders or dozers, and no validated occupant-injury curve for automatic-braking events: **not found**.

facts.text: Reports of operator jarring during automatic stops support testing deceleration and jerk, not just stopping distance.
facts.quote: Reported, not measured. Supports testing deceleration and jerk, not just stopping distance. **Independent**

facts.text: No quantified off-road data linking automatic braking to spilled payload, falling rock or load shift was found.
facts.quote: **Not found**: no quantified off-road data linking automatic braking to spilled payload, falling rock or load shift.

facts.text: Spilled or shifted loads from automatic braking are a mechanically credible hazard for loaded dumpers, loaders and machines with raised implements.
facts.quote: The hazard is mechanically credible for loaded dumpers, loaders and machines with raised implements.

facts.text: Queensland requires separation and stopping judgments to consider fully laden vehicles and worst road conditions.
facts.quote: Queensland already requires separation and stopping judgments to consider fully laden vehicles and worst road conditions [14].

facts.text: Spilled or shifted loads should be treated as a hazard-analysis and test item covering laden and unladen machines and implement positions, not as an established automatic-braking failure rate.
facts.quote: Gap; a hazard-analysis and test item (laden and unladen, implement positions), not an established failure rate. **Independent** (guidance)

facts.text: MOSH guidance says braking performance depends on gradient, side slope and braking system response time.
facts.quote: MOSH guidance says braking performance depends on "gradient and side slope" and "braking system response time", and ISO/TS 21815-2 separates emergency stops from controlled stops [20, 82].

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 separates emergency stops from controlled stops.
facts.quote: ISO/TS 21815-2 separates emergency stops from controlled stops [20, 82].

facts.text: Queensland requires stopping-distance assumptions to cover the worst relevant combination of wet or slippery road, downhill grade, maximum speed, fully laden vehicle, poor tyre condition, fatigue or distraction, and mechanical brake delay.
facts.quote: Queensland requires stopping-distance assumptions to cover the worst relevant combination of wet or slippery road, downhill grade, maximum speed, fully laden vehicle, poor tyre condition, fatigue or distraction and mechanical brake delay [14].

facts.text: NIOSH links berm deaths to loss of control and excessive speed on grades over 9%.
facts.quote: NIOSH links berm deaths to loss of control and to excessive speed on grades over 9% [4].

facts.text: Direct evidence that automatic braking has caused a rollover or slope instability was not found; quantified incidents were not found despite recognition of the risk in guidance.
facts.quote: Direct evidence that automatic braking has caused a rollover or slope instability: **not found**.

facts.text: Whether a machine should use full braking, staged braking, speed reduction or propulsion inhibit depends on the machine and conditions and cannot be inferred from accident data alone.
facts.quote: Whether a machine should apply full braking, staged braking, speed reduction or propulsion inhibit is machine- and condition-dependent and cannot be inferred from accident data alone.

facts.text: Evidence of a following vehicle striking an automatically braked machine was not found in mining sources.
facts.quote: | A following vehicle striking the braked machine | **Not found** in mining sources.

facts.text: A following vehicle striking an automatically braked machine is a credible risk in convoys, queues and approach situations.
facts.quote: The risk is credible in convoys, queues and approach situations.

facts.text: In US insurance data, FCW with automatic emergency braking raised the rate of being struck from behind by 20%, according to Cicchino (2017); this is on-road evidence only.
facts.quote: FCW with automatic emergency braking (AEB) raised the rate of being struck from behind by 20% in US insurance data (Cicchino, 2017) [23]. **Independent (on-road evidence)**

facts.text: The risk of a following vehicle striking an automatically braked machine belongs in scenario-based validation where site rules allow close following; the cited incident-rate evidence is on-road only.
facts.quote: On-road only; belongs in scenario-based validation where site rules allow close following

facts.text: An unnamed machine manufacturer told MSHA in the Federal Register of 9 January 2017 that field testing with US coal customers showed section production tonnage drops within five to ten percent of normal production levels when proximity detection was active on haulage equipment.
facts.quote: "measurable section production tonnage drops, within five to ten percent of normal production levels, when proximity detection is active on haulage equipment"

facts.text: Two mine operators told MSHA that production returned to normal, contrasting with an unnamed manufacturer's report of production drops when proximity detection was active.
facts.quote: two mine operators said production returned to normal [22].

facts.text: Mobile PDS was rated less favorably on task completion, reliability, safety and compatibility.
facts.quote: Mobile PDS was rated less favorably on task completion, reliability, safety and compatibility;

facts.text: Loading, troubleshooting, maintenance and inspections became harder with mobile PDS.
facts.quote: loading, troubleshooting, maintenance and inspections became harder [12].

facts.text: No defensible percentage productivity penalty for surface automatic braking was found.
facts.quote: No defensible percentage penalty for surface automatic braking: **not found**.

facts.text: A system that stops a machine dozens of times a shift creates an incentive to widen zones, disable alarms, override braking or develop informal workarounds, linking productivity to safety behavior.
facts.quote: a system that stops the machine dozens of times a shift creates an incentive to widen zones, disable alarms, override braking or develop informal workarounds.
